| Regulatory basis | • Residential areas should provide all four container categories. Food-waste and residual-waste bins should be grouped by entrance or building, preferably at a 1:1–1:3 ratio. Enclosed developments need at least one hazardous-waste and one recyclables point, with more in larger developments; open residential areas need these containers per 300–500 households. Food and residual bins should be near entrances; combined recyclables/residual units in recreation areas; residual bins in toilets; and hazardous/recyclables containers at suitable main entrances, routes, activity areas or underground garages. Wuhan Guidelines for Municipal Solid Waste Classification in Major Settings, Section 4.5.4, [D-16-C004](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• The guidance covers waste reduction, classified disposal and collection, and related management in nine Wuhan settings, including residential areas. Wuhan Guidelines for Municipal Solid Waste Classification in Major Settings, Section 1.2, [D-16-C001](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Failure to maintain functional, intact classification containers must be corrected; failure to meet the deadline attracts CNY 1,000–3,000 fines. Wuhan Municipal Measures for Municipal Solid Waste Classification, Article 18, items (1), [D-08-C011](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Failure to store waste at compliant collection locations or transfer it to compliant collectors must be corrected; failure to meet the deadline attracts CNY 5,000–50,000 fines for organisations. Wuhan Municipal Measures for Municipal Solid Waste Classification, Article 18, items (2), [D-08-C011](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Failure to classify waste at designated locations requires correction; refusal attracts CNY 50,000–500,000 fines for organisations and CNY 100–1,000 for individuals. Wuhan Municipal Measures for Municipal Solid Waste Classification, Article 18, items (3), [D-08-C011](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Mixing previously classified waste during collection or transport must be corrected; failure to meet the deadline attracts CNY 5,000–30,000 fines for collection enterprises. Wuhan Municipal Measures for Municipal Solid Waste Classification, Article 18, items (4), [D-08-C011](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Failure to follow classified treatment requirements must be corrected; continued non-compliance attracts CNY 30,000–50,000 fines for disposal organisations and compensation for losses. Wuhan Municipal Measures for Municipal Solid Waste Classification, Article 18, items (5), [D-08-C011](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Indiscriminate dumping, scattering or stockpiling must cease and be corrected; fines are CNY 5,000–50,000 for organisations and up to CNY 200 for individuals. Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste, Article 42, [D-03-C007](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Commercial cleaning, collection and transport enterprises failing to fulfil duties must correct the problem and may be fined CNY 5,000–30,000; disposal enterprises may be fined CNY 30,000–100,000. Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste, Article 45, [D-03-C010](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv). |
| Severity | **Moderate.** Although no conventional bins are identified, two overflow labels are attached to non-standard containers—an inverted stool and a pot—used for temporary waste storage. Clutter and absent classification facilities indicate management gaps. No obvious pollution or accumulation is evident, but container requirements are unmet and improper disposal is possible. |
| Impact assessment | Visible effects: non-standard containers used for storage may encourage littering and weaken classification awareness. Near-term risks include confusion over disposal locations, scattering if containers overturn or blow away, and insect breeding in stones and twigs in the pot. |
| Potential causes | • Non-compliant bin provision may leave residents without disposal facilities and encourage use of pots or stools: no classification bins are visible and overflow labels identify non-standard containers.<br>• Managers may fail to provide or maintain containers or remove waste promptly. Verify facility records, collection registers and responsible persons’ performance records.<br>• Limited resident awareness and guidance may encourage stockpiling. Observe disposal behaviour, signs and supervision. |
| Long-term effects | Persistent or recurrent problems could impede classification habits and participation, occupy public space and obstruct passage, cause odours and insect breeding through delayed collection, increase disease risks and expose managers to penalties and reputational harm. |
| Recommendations | • Immediate action: remove non-standard containers and surrounding items in S12-B-01 and S12-B-02, restore cleanliness, provide clearly labelled four-category bins for food waste, residual waste, recyclables and hazardous waste, and assign checks to prevent recurrence.<br>• Longer-term action: audit Yanzhi Road Community’s facilities against Section 4.5.4 of the Wuhan Guidelines for Municipal Solid Waste Classification in Major Settings; promote classification through noticeboards and household guidance; and establish regular checks and collection with clear responsibilities. |
| Priority | **High.** Missing classification facilities, non-standard waste containers and clutter violate basic provision requirements and could encourage improper disposal, sanitation risks and management liability. Correct promptly to prevent escalation. |
